description: A passionate Software Engineering (RPL) student from Indonesia exploring space data solutions using modern development frameworks and AI assistance
summary:
ISS Expedition 74 // Crew Biomedical Telemetry Console is an offline-first, autonomous onboard health monitoring and clinical decision-support application engineered for astronauts on long-duration spaceflight missions. Built in strict compliance with the Astro User Experience Design System (Astro UXDS) aerospace telemetry standard, the console addresses the critical challenge of Earth-communication latency during deep-space missions, where crews cannot rely solely on real-time ground flight surgeons to detect and mitigate physiological anomalies.

The system synthesizes multi-crew physiological streams across cardiovascular telemetry, microgravity bone mineral density (BMD) resorption, ionizing radiation flux, circadian sleep alignment, and behavioral isolation stress. By translating raw biomedical data into high-glanceability status tokens, interactive 7-Sol trend analytics, and guided countermeasure protocols—such as a 4-7-8 vagal breathing pacer, ARED resistive exercise tracking, and automated medical SOAP downlink packets—the console empowers astronauts to self-monitor and maintain peak mission readiness independently.
details:
How It Works & Key Capabilities: Designed as a single-viewport, zero-clutter dark-mode telemetry console (#101923 Deep Space Blue and #4DACFF Aerospace Cyan), the application monitors four ISS Expedition 74 crew members (CREW-01 through CREW-04) simultaneously against live Mission Elapsed Time (MET). It tracks three core operational pillars:

  1. Vital Signs & Biometrics: Real-time BPM-synchronized cardiovascular telemetry (Heart Rate, Blood Pressure, HRV), Bone & Muscle Density (BMD delta and daily ARED load progress), and Immune & Radiation exposure (mSv cumulative dose and daily solar flux) with interactive hover sparklines and subsystem deep-dive modals.
  2. Behavioral & Sleep Analytics: Tracks 7-Sol sleep duration against an 8.0-hour target, circadian synchronization percentage, and confinement stress load.
  3. Autonomous AI Decision Support & Guided Execution: Evaluates multi-system risk corridors locally to generate diagnostic summaries and executable countermeasure checklists with built-in tactical countdown timers that update biometric recovery upon completion. A slide-over control drawer provides a 0.5 Hz live sensor simulator, manual parameter overrides, symptom self-reporting, a chronological audit log, and JSON SOAP medical downlink export.

Tools, Tech Stack & Design Factors: Developed using React 18, Tailwind CSS (configured with Astro UXDS design tokens), custom technical SVG iconography, Inter and JetBrains Mono typography, modular vanilla JavaScript, and optional Google Gemini API integration. To maximize operational resilience, energy efficiency, and accessibility in spacecraft environments, the application is lightweight, offline-first with zero mandatory cloud dependencies during communication blackouts, and engineered for rapid glanceability under high-stress conditions.
